text.tspan: The pipeline begins with a natural language description specifying
the target mobile application's interface and behavior.
The input text is tokenized and preprocessed, separating literal strings
into placeholder tokens to reduce model overhead.
The preprocessed sequence is then passed into the encoder
The decoder sequentially generates the formal structural representation of the application.
This output forms a compact intermediate representation called
the Simplified App Representation, or SAR.
Next, the SAR Compiler parses the tokens and maps them
The compiler re-inserts the original string literals to produce
MIT App Inventor source files (.scm and .bky).
These source files are sent to the MIT App Inventor backend compiler
to build the project into an Android package.
The result is a fully functional, ready-to-use Android application package (.apk).
